summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with worsening dyspnea, found to have acute renal failure, hypercalcemia, and an elevated INR of 16. The hypercalcemia, secondary to multiple myeloma progression, was treated with IV fluids, pamidronate, calcitonin, and steroids, leading to subsequent hypocalcemia managed with aggressive calcium and vitamin D repletion. His renal function improved with hydration, and Coumadin was held then restarted after INR normalization with FFP and vitamin K. A urinary tract infection with Enterococcus was treated with antibiotics. His respiratory symptoms resolved with a course of vancomycin, cefepime, and azithromycin, supported by improving CT findings. Revlimid was resumed as renal function recovered. He was discharged home ambulatory with plans for close outpatient follow-up for calcium monitoring, oncology care, and anticoagulation management.
